description: A clock multiplier that runs only while it is switched on, so a steady clock can be broken into bursts of faster pulses

params.text: How many steps a burst started by ON or TOGGLE runs for before stopping itself, a whole number from 1 to 64
Scales the voltage at the STEPS input before it is added to the STEPS knob, inverting it left of centre; at full, 10V covers the whole 1 to 64 range
Scales the voltage at the MULTI input before it is added to the MULTI knob, inverting it left of centre; at full, 10V covers the whole 1 to 16 range
How many pulses the burst puts out for each incoming clock, a whole number from 1 to 16
Multiplies the MULTI setting by four, taking the burst as high as 64 pulses to the clock

inputs.text: Adds to the MULTI knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to 1 to 16 and rounded to a whole number
Adds to the STEPS knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to 1 to 64 and rounded to a whole number
Holds the burst on for as long as the voltage here stays at or above 1V
A rising edge above 1V starts the burst if it is off and stops it if it is on, and sets the step count back to zero either way
A rising edge above 1V stops the burst and sets the step count back to zero
A rising edge above 1V starts the burst and sets the step count back to zero
A rising edge above 1V counts one step, and the burst stops itself once STEPS of them have arrived; edges are counted only for a burst started by ON or TOGGLE, not for one held on by the GATE input
The clock being multiplied; the interval between two rising edges above 1V is the tempo everything else is worked out from

outputs.text: The step count as a voltage, climbing from 0V towards 10V as the count fills
A 1ms pulse on each incoming clock edge, but only while the burst is off
10V for as long as the burst is on, and 0V while it is off
A 1ms pulse at each beat of the multiplied rate, and nothing at all while the burst is off
A 1ms pulse on every incoming clock edge, with the multiplied beats added while the burst is on
A 1ms pulse at the moment the burst ends, however it was ended

notes: every output is timed from the gap between two rising edges at CLOCK, so nothing comes out until a clock is patched there and has ticked twice.
the burst comes up off when a patch is loaded, so SOLO is silent until ON, TOGGLE or a high GATE starts it.
the multiplied beats stop once a whole clock interval has gone by with no new edge, so a clock that stops leaves the module silent rather than free-running.
